samples: This module models roles as named sets of permissions, each written as resource:action, and offers helpers to combine roles, list which required permissions no role grants, check whether all requirements are met, and find the permissions two roles share. It is pure set logic with no storage or external access, so it could be reused as a small authorization check. Its demo program checks a sample viewer and editor against a three-permission publishing requirement, so it prints that the publish permission is missing, then prints the one permission the two roles share (reading posts).

This module is a small authorization library: it models permissions as validated "resource:action" names (lowercase letters, with underscores allowed in the action) and roles as named sets of them. It offers pure functions to pool what several roles grant, list which required permissions are missing, check whether all of them are covered, and find what two roles share. Its demo program checks a sample viewer and editor against a publishing requirement, and prints that the publish permission is missing and that the two roles share only read access, so it is a reusable building block rather than a full access-control system.

This module is a small authorization library. It models permissions as validated "resource:action" names and roles as named sets of them, and it offers functions to pool what several roles grant, list which required permissions are missing, check whether all requirements are met, and find the permissions two roles share. Its demo program checks a sample viewer and editor against a publishing requirement and prints that the one missing permission is the publish permission, because neither role grants it. It then prints the single permission the two roles share, which is the read permission; it only prints to the console and touches no files or network.

This module lets you check whether a group of roles, each holding a set of permissions written as "resource:action" (for example, orders:read), together covers everything an action requires. It offers functions to combine the roles' grants, list which required permissions are still missing, give a yes/no answer on whether all are covered, and find the permissions two roles have in common. Its demo checks a sample viewer and editor against a publishing requirement and prints that publish permission is missing, then that the one shared permission is posts:read.

This is a small authorization library that models roles as named sets of permissions written as resource:action (for example orders:read), and answers questions about them: what a group of roles grants together, which required permissions are missing, whether everything required is covered, and which permissions two roles share. Its demo checks a viewer (read only) and an editor (read and write) against what publishing needs (read, write and publish). Because nobody holds the publish permission, it prints that publish is missing, followed by the one permission the two roles share, which is read.
